content.title: Overview
content.body:
Times are changing...

The bravery of adventurers is needed once again. Blackriver, a county of the Kingdom of Elan, has been suffering with the kidnapping of villagers under the cover of night. People are frightened, and monstrous silhouettes wander in the darkness, gnashing teeth and claws.

You arrived late, from far away. In the twilight gloom, wherever you look, desolation and bloodstains paint the walls and alleys red. There’s no sign of your contractor. Or of any living soul, really. Those who remain have locked themselves inside their homes, praying for a miracle.

There is no mystery here: All tracks lead to the Count’s fortress, and whatever is happening there must be what you were hired to stop.

Or rather, to fight...

Overview

This tutorial will teach you how to play CoD through a gameplay-centered approach.

Learning combines rules explanations with gameplay instructions, spread throughout the Adventure, which should take three sessions of Drunagor Nights. The goal is simple but ambitious: by the end of this experience, you will have learned to play without having to read the entire Rulebook.

The first few rooms contain more Lessons, but as the Party progresses, explanations take up less space and Gameplay takes center stage.

First, each player flips their Hero Board to the “Tutorial” side (the one with the gray boxes).

Make sure you are using the Tutorial version of your Hero Board.

Next, for this Tutorial to work, one Hero must pick the “DEFENDER” Role.

  • If no Hero has the DEFENDER Dungeon Role, assign it to one of them.
    • Swap their Dungeon Roles I and II cards.
    • Move their Initiative card to the first slot on the Initiative Track.
    • That Hero increases his Maximum Health by 4, due to the DEFENDER's "Constitution" Passive Ability.

Once a Hero has the DEFENDER Dungeon Role, you’re ready. Without further ado, let’s get started!

content.title: Your First Turns
content.body:
Assembling a Setup

A Setup is a “room” in the Dungeon.

Each Setup is shown as a 2D illustration indicating which Trays, Maps, and Doors to place on the board.

Each Adventure begins with the First Setup. Let’s build it.

  • Start by placing Trays, Maps, and Doors as shown below. Maps have codes to help you identify them. Likewise, each Door shows its number and the Adventure it belongs to.

The First Setup is shown on one side, and its Trays, Maps, and Doors arranged on the board are shown on the other.

Now, let’s "populate" the board. Each Setup diagram shows which Miniatures to place and how many of each, based on the number of Heroes in the Party.

This is the First Setup's diagram.

So, for a Party of three Heroes, you would have to place all elements unmarked (such as the Starting Positions); all elements marked 2+; and all marked 3+.

The First Setup contains Monsters: the Vampire. To populate a Setup with Monsters, follow the three steps below. You can complete each step as you read it.

1) Place their Monster card in the indicated position on the Initiative Track.

This is where the Vampire card goes on the Initiative Track.

2) Attach colored bases to the models and place them on the board.

Taking a Party of 2 Heroes as an example, 2 Vampires are placed. When playing your own session, make sure to place the correct number of Vampires for the number of Heroes in your Party, in the positions shown in the Setup.

3) Mark each Monster’s Health on the Monster Status Board, using White Cubes.

Again, this example uses a Party of 2 Heroes. Make sure to track the Health of every miniature required for your Party size.

At last, the First Setup also shows the Heroes’ Starting Positions (the asterisks). These are the Squares where the Heroes’ models are placed to begin the Adventure.

  • Next, each player places their Hero’s model in a Starting Position of their choice.

These are the Heroes’ starting positions in the First Setup.

Now that we’ve covered how to assemble the board, let’s explore CoD’s game mechanics, starting with the Round manegement.

Turns and Rounds

Chronicles of Drunagor is played over a series of turns and rounds. A turn is when a Character takes Actions during a round. The Initiative Track organizes this process.

This is the Initiative Track and Marker.

The turn order runs from left to right and from the top to the bottom of the track, as if it were a long straight line.

When the Initiative Marker reaches a card, that Character or Event takes its turn. Once that turn ends, move the marker to the next card.

After preparing the Heroes and building the Setup, there are now cards on the Initiative Track.

  • Place the Initiative Marker (it is a large token) on the first card on the Initiative Track, the Hero playing the DEFENDER Role.

The example uses Vorn as the DEFENDER, but make sure the Initiative Marker is on the correct Hero’s card for your Party.

Hero Turn

Heroes can take the following Actions during their turn, alternating between them as they choose:

  • Take up to one Free Move Action
  • Take up to two Cube Actions

Free Move Action

The Free Move Action is the basic way Heroes move in CoD. It grants 3 movement points.

  • Each square moved into costs 1 movement point.
  • Diagonal movement does not cost additional points.
  • Move between board levels does not cost additional points, as long as the difference is only one level.

Heroes can move through (but not stop in) squares occupied by their allies. However, they cannot move through squares occupied by enemies.

Cube Action

Cube Actions are essentially how Heroes use their Skills. To take a Cube Action, spend an Action Cube of the appropriate color, placing it in that Skill’s slot.

Spending an Action Cube means docking it to a Skill slot.

The color of the Cube determines the Range for all effects of that Skill, including Attacks ():

  • Melee (yellow): Targets Characters adjacent to the Hero.

This is an example of Melee Range.

  • Ranged (red): Targets Characters within Range 1, that is, in any square in the same area (blue square) or in an area adjacent to the one the Hero is in.

This is an example of Range 1.

  • Agility (green) or Wisdom (blue): Targets Characters anywhere on the board.

This is an example of Unlimited Range.

  • A Hero is always within the Range of any effects they cast themselves.

Now, let’s put this into practice.

  • Consider your Hero's combat style.
    • Melee Heroes begin the Adventure with 2 yellow Action Cubes; Ranged Heroes begin with 2 red Action Cubes.
  • Take a Free Move Action to get within Range to attack the Vampire.
    • Melee Heroes must be adjacent to the Vampire.
    • Ranged Heroes must be within Range 1 of the Vampire, but not adjacent to it.

These are movement options for Melee and Ranged Heroes, respectively.

Then, let’s take our first Cube Action.

  • Choose one of your Skills with a “”.
  • Spend an Action Cube of the appropriate color to cast that Skill.
    • You can find the effects of the main KEYWORDS used by your Hero on their Hero Board.

Once you’re ready to resolve (after understanding and applying any other effects of your Attack), proceed to the next Lesson.

Making Weapon Attacks

Weapon Attack instructions follow the pattern “MAKE A OF +X TO HIT”. To make a , Roll the D20 and add any TO HIT bonuses (+X TO HIT) to the result.

If the Roll equals or exceeds your Weapon’s Accuracy (blue diamond), the Attack hits. “Natural” 20’s (value shown in the dice), are Critical Hits—It deals double damage. “Natural” 1's are Critical Failures—They miss.

Taking Arcing Strike as an example, Vorn must roll at least a 4 on the D20 for the Attack to hit, since his Skill grants +3 TO HIT and his Weapon has Accuracy 7.

If the Attack hits, the yellow Vampire takes 3 damage.

Now, it’s up to you.

  • Make your Attack Roll ().
    • If your Attack hits, reduce the Vampire’s Health accordingly.
    • For the purposes of this Lesson, you will end your turn without taking any further Actions.
  • Move the Initiative Marker to the next card on the Track, the Vampire, beginning its turn.

The Monsters’ Turn

When the Initiative Marker reaches a Monster card, every miniature of that Monster type takes its turn.

This time, ACTIVATE 1 Vampire that can reach a Hero. That Vampire moves (if necessary) and attacks. Even if there are 2 or more Vampires on the board, only 1 will be ACTIVATED this turn.

ACTIVATING a Monster is done by following four steps. You can complete each step as you read it.

1) First, any Conditions affecting the Monster are triggered.

  • A Monster will only have Conditions at this point if the DEFENDER is Elros and has hit it with “Poisonous Strike,” inflicting POISON 2.

2) Secondly, they “aim” at their Target.

The Vampire targets the STRONGEST HERO.

  • Monsters only target Heroes they can reach.
  • STRONGEST HERO is the Hero with the most Health at the moment. In the event of ties, who acts first in the Initiative Track is the STRONGEST HERO between two Heroes.
  • If they cannot reach any Heroes, Monsters will just move to get as close to one as possible.

3) Third, they move towards their Target, if necessary.

  • Monsters follow the shortest path possible.
  • The amount of Movement Points that each Monster has per Turn is shown on its card.

4) Finally, they attack.

  • Monsters do not roll the D20; They always hit, dealing the damage described on their card.

The Vampire’s Attack deals damage, but Heroes can take Reactions. Do not reduce their Health yet.

Reactions

Reactions () are used only when a Hero is Threatened—that is, when any Hero is attacked.

To React, the Hero also spends an Action Cube. Reactions, however, do not count as Cube Actions. Even if a Hero has taken or not their turn yet, they can still use as many Reactions as they want.

To use Parry, Vorn must spend 1 Agility Action Cube.

Each Hero can only use 1 Reaction per Threat.

Damage dealt to Heroes who have SHIELD tokens discard them first. If the damage is reduced to 0, no Threat is generated and no Reaction can be taken.

Heroes can React to Threats to other Heroes, but only if their Reaction can choose “ANY TARGET”.

Vorn’s Parry can only be used to protect himself. Jaheen’s Intervention, on the other hand, can be used to protect any Hero (including himself).

So, imagine that Vorn is being attacked by the Vampire and uses “PARRY”. This Skill casts PREVENT on him equal to his Weapon’s Damage (3).

Parry PREVENTS 3 of the 6 Damage dealt by the Vampire.

Vorn therefore loses 3 Health.

Now, let’s practice using Reactions ().

  • Use one of your Hero’s Reactions.
    • For the purposes of this tutorial, do not use other Heroes’ Reactions. Let your Hero take some of the Damage and reduce their Health accordingly.

Moving on, we need to program the next Lesson and continue with this round.

  • Place the Recall Actions Tutorial Trigger (1) card at the bottom end of the Initiative Track.

Game system cards (Game State Check-Up, Rune, or Tutorial Trigger cards) are placed at the end of the Initiative Track, in the lower section of the Rune Slot, making them the last cards to ACTIVATE each round.

  • Continue the round by moving the Initiative Marker to the next card on the Initiative Track.
    • There is probably at least one more Hero left to act this round. These Heroes take their turns, taking Cube Actions and Move Actions as they wish. They may even kill a Vampire.
  • Eventually, the Initiative Marker will reach the Recall Actions Tutorial Trigger card, prompting you to read the next Lesson.

Managing the turn sequence until the end of the round is your first challenge! The next lessons, indicated by the Tutorial Trigger card, can be found on the following pages.

You may leave this book aside for now and focus on the gameplay.

HINT: Heroes can take additional Move Actions: they discard 1 Action Cube from their Pool, placing it in their “Expended Cubes Box” on their Hero Board. Each time they do, it counts as one Cube Action.

content.title: Recall Actions
content.body:
Recall Action

Heroes will eventually run out of Action Cubes. They can take Recall Actions to replenish them.

Recall Actions can be Willing or Unwilling.

Willing Recall Actions can be taken by a Hero during their turn if their available Action Cubes are of two or fewer colors. If a Hero does so, their turn ends.

Unwilling Recall Actions are triggered when a Hero spends their last available Action Cube during any turn. This does not end the current turn.

Regardless of its type, when taking a Recall Action, the Hero returns all their Action Cubes back to their Pool.

This is an example of a Recall Action.

Recall Actions are not free: Heroes receive 1 Curse Cube as penalty whenever they take one.

Vorn took a Recall Action and therefore received 1 Curse Cube. Curse Cubes are the black cubes.

Curse Cubes

Curse Cubes represents exhaustion.

Once received, these Cubes must be placed on one of the Hero’s Skills, blocking its use.

Curse Cubes remain on the Hero’s Board until removed by CLEANSE effects.

Vorn has blocked Hammer Throw with the Curse Cube he received after taking a Recall Action.

Now, it's time to move on. Let’s prepare for our next Lessons and learning activities.

  • Replace the Recall Actions Tutorial Trigger card with the Folding Doors (2) at the end of the Track.

The Tutorial Trigger cards were replaced on the Track.

  • Place the End of the Round Game State Check-Up card also at the end of the Track, just below the Folding Doors Tutorial Trigger card.
    • Whenever a slot on the Initiative Track contains more than one card, ACTIVATE every card in that slot, starting with the card at the top.

After following these two instructions, your Initiative Track should have these two cards in the Rune Slot.

  • Move the Marker back to the first card on the Track, the Hero with the “DEFENDER” role.
  • Play the next rounds from the first card to the last on the Track, ACTIVATING each Hero and each Monster normally.

This is free play, so Heroes may move, use Skills, make Attacks, take Reactions, and Recall Actions as they wish.

Managing the gameplay for as many rounds as it takes to kill all the Vampires and let the Tutorial Trigger card guide you to the next Lesson is your second challenge!

You may leave this book aside for now and focus on the gameplay.

content.title: Folding Doors
content.body:
Folding Doors

Dungeon crawling is all about exploration. Each Door reveals new locations and challenges.

In Drunagor Nights, Doors can only be opened at the end of the round. To open a Door, a Hero must be adjacent to it and choose to do so when the Game State Check Up card ACTIVATES.

Doors cannot be opened as long as there are Monsters alive.

Let's open our first Door.

  • First, each Hero repositions their model in one of the squares on Map DNE2-F. At least one Hero must be in a square adjacent to the Door.

Vorn repositioned his model adjacent to the Door.

  • Next, remove the Folding Doors Tutorial Trigger card and ACTIVATE the End of the Round Game-State Check-Up card.
    • Since no Monsters remain alive and at least one Hero is adjacent to the next Door, it opens.
    • Take the Door card, unfold it, then read its Special Rules.

Start by reading the story text (if you wish), then read the Special Rules, leaving the Setup for later.

When you read that Door’s Special Rules, you will be directed to the next Lesson – “Populating a Room”.

content.title: Populating a Room
content.body:
Populating a Room

Doors reveal the next Setup. Assembling and populating a Setup were covered at the beginning of this Tutorial, but here’s a reminder. You can complete each step as you read it.

1) Start by assembling the Trays, Maps, and Doors.

  • The yellow arrow indicates where the new Setup connects to the previous one.

The yellow arrow points to the Area where the two Setups should connect.

2) Place each Monster card in the indicated position on the Track.

This is where the Archer and the Rotten goes on the Initiative Track.

3) Place each Monster model in the indicated positions on the board, attaching a colored base to each.

Again, according to the Setup diagram, 2 Monsters of each type are placed on the board for a Party of 2 Heroes. Make sure to place the appropriate Monsters for your Party size.

4) Mark the Health of each Monster on the Monster Status board. The value is indicated on their cards.

Each Archer has 8 Health, while each Rotten has 12 Health.

HINT: At this point, you may remove the Vampire’s Monster card from the Initiative Track if you wish.

Ranged Monsters

Some Monsters can Attack from a distance. This does not change their overall behavior, but it does introduce some new things you must consider:

Ranged Monsters can attack enemies up to 1 area (blue square) away.

Ranged Monsters can’t attack enemies if a Hero is adjacent to them. This is called Combat Engagement.

Ranged Monsters that are Engaged in Combat will move away from the Heroes who are obstructing their attack whenever necessary.

Ranged Monsters that cannot leave Combat Engagement during an ACTIVATION do not attack.

So, let's begin the second encounter.

  • Place the Interaction Tutorial Trigger (3) card at the bottom end of the Initiative Track, on top of the Barricade Game State Check-Up card.

The Interactions Tutorial Trigger card goes on top of the Barricade Game State Check-Up card.

  • Play the next rounds until you kill all the Monsters. When the Tutorial Trigger card is ACTIVATED during the round, you will be instructed to read the next Lesson if no Monsters remain alive.
    • This time, killing all the Monsters will take longer: 2, 3, or even more rounds.

Once again, this is a free-play section of the tutorial.

Managing the gameplay until every Monster is killed and the Initiative Marker reaches the Tutorial Trigger card at the end of the round is your third challenge!

You may leave this book aside for now and focus on the gameplay.

NOTE: The Rotten Monster has a Passive Ability: “Attack Twice”, which means that it takes two Attack Actions when ACTIVATED (but only a single Move Action).

content.title: Interactions
content.body:
Interaction

Interactions are dilemmas where the players can affect the story in many ways, positive or negative.

  • The Hero inspecting the Interaction chooses one of the resolutions.
  • Each resolution can only be chosen once, even if a different Hero is able to inspect that same Interaction later.

Interactions can grant Items or cause changes to the narrative and gameplay.

Items I

Items come in two types:

  • 1)Equipment, the gear a Hero can wield;
  • Check your Hero’s proficiencies—They can only wield Equipment of those types.
  • 2) Consumable Items, single-use findings.
  • When a Consumable Item is used, the player discards its card.

Each Hero’s Bag can carry up to two Items at a time. If a third Item is placed in it, the player must discard one of the three cards.

These Lessons help you manage the rewards from the Interaction you are about to inspect. First, however, follow these steps to reach it:

  • Remove the Interactions Tutorial Trigger card from the Initiative Track.
  • Then, each Hero and Pet repositions their model in a square of their choice on Map DNE4-F. At least one Hero must be adjacent to the Door.

Reposition the Characters in any Squares on the Map, but place at least one Hero adjacent to the next Door.

  • At last, ACTIVATE the Barricade Game State Check-Up card.
    • It instructs you to open the next Door, but not immediately. First, the Hero adjacent to it proceeds to the Interaction – “The Barricade”.

The button below opens the Interaction. Once it opens, examine the scene, read the accompanying text, and click on a Resolution to choose it.

The next Lesson will be presented once the Party completes its Inspection.

You may leave this book aside for now and focus on the gameplay.

content.title: Skills and Commanders
content.body:
Learning New Skills

From time to time, Heroes learn new Skills and Abilities to better prepare for upcoming challenges.

Heroes can only learn Hero Skills on their own cards.

Each Hero Skill card has two sides—The front side corresponds to Level 1 of that Skill while the back corresponds to Level 2.

Whenever a Hero learns or upgrades a Skill, they receive 1 Action Cube of the color associated with that Skill.

Now, let's learn our first Skill.

  • Each Hero learns a new Level 1 Skill.
    • Remember to collect the appropriate Action Cubes from the Reserve. Each Hero now has a Pool of 6 Action Cubes.

Commanders

Commanders are Monsters with special game mechanics, functioning as “Mini-Bosses” in an Adventure.

They are placed on the board like any other Monster, but there are a few additional steps. Let’s start with the ones we already know. Complete each step as you read it.

  • Place its Monster card on the Initiative Track. Commanders have golden background.
  • Place its model in the indicated position on the board, attaching a colored base to it.
  • Set the Commander's Health on the Monster Status Board.
    • The Guardian will have 16, 32, 48, or 64 Health, depending on the number of Heroes. If needed, use the +30 HP tokens or additional Tracks.

Now, let’s move on to what’s new. Commanders gain extra Actions each round, the Attack cards.

These are the Commander Attack cards.

Attack cards explain their own effects, like a Skill. “X” equals the number of Runes of that color on the Track. Attack cards are ACTIVATED just like any other card: when the Initiative Marker reaches them on the Track.

  • Draw a Hand of Attack Cards for the Commander Guardian (1 card for each Hero in the Party), placing them on the Initiative Track.

This is an example of an Attack card hand for 3 Heroes.

Large Monsters

The Guardian is also a Large Monster, and its size imposes some special rules.

Large Monsters move from area to area. So, 2 movement points means they can cross 2 areas. Large Monsters may move through or stop in areas occupied by smaller Monsters and/or Chests. Large Monsters cannot stop in areas occupied by Heroes, NPC tokens, or Pets.

When a Large Monster attacks a Hero, it also attacks every other Hero, NPC, or Pet in the same Area as that Hero. Large Monsters prioritize hitting as many Heroes as they can over hitting the Strongest Hero.

At last, large Monsters are Immune to KNOCK DOWN, PUSH, STUN, and TELEKINESIS. These Immunities are represented by the “LARGE” icon.

Now, it's up to you to face this challenge.

  • Play the next rounds until you kill the Commander Guardian.

Once again, this is a free-play section of the tutorial.

The next Lesson will be presented when Door 3 is opened. The goal here is to defeat the Commander and open the next Door without a Lesson guiding you.

At last, for this tutorial, however, the Commander has a handicap. Treat any value written as “X” on its Attack cards as “Half of X (rounded down).” Also, remember: the Special Rule – “Plot Armor” is still in effect.

So, you may leave this book aside for now and focus on the gameplay.

content.title: Minor Actions
content.body:
Minor Actions

Heroes may take a third type of Action: the Minor Action. Heroes may take one of each of these actions during their turn to perform special tasks such as:

1) Loot a Chest.

  • The Hero draws the top Chest card from the deck.

2) Give 1 Item from their Bag to another Hero.

  • Bags are magical—There is no Range limit.

3) Equip, Unequip, or Exchange Equipment.

  • Heroes do not need to have free space in their Bags to Exchange Equipment.

4) Inspect an Interaction token.

5) Any other effects described as a “Minor Action”.

Some Special Events or Class Abilities perform effects at the cost of a Minor Action.

Later on, Heroes will learn to use what are called “Focus Abilities.” Using one of these Abilities—if it’s not marked as a Reaction ()—also counts as a Minor Action.

Interaction Tokens

Sometimes, Interactions can be represented by tokens on the board. Inspecting them is a Minor Action taken by an adjacent Hero.

When a Hero does so, open the QR Code scanner in the Drunagor App and scan the code. The Hero chooses a Resolution and follows its instructions.

When the Interaction is complete, reduce the charges of that token by 1. If that was the last charge, remove the token from the board.

Interaction tokens are Solid Objects. Characters cannot pass through (unless they are JUMPING) or end their movement on them.

Darkness Nodes

Piles of Runes represent Darkness Nodes are storages of pure power. They are represented by Piles of Runes, formed by taking 1 Rune of each color from the Track.

Piles of Runes are Solid Objects. Characters cannot pass through or end their movement on them.

Form the Pile by taking 1 Rune of each color from the Initiative Track.

Let's put all this into practice. Assemble a Pile of Runes.

  • Place a Pile of Runes in the indicated Square.

Tie Breaker

Heroes, in turn, can destroy the Darkness Nodes, through the Special Action “Tie Breaker”.

To do so, the Hero must be adjacent to the Pile of Runes and must Expend 1 AC (move it to the Expended Cube box). This counts as one Cube Action.

When they do, they choose a number of Runes equal to 6 minus the number of Heroes in the Party and returns them to the bag. That Hero also receives CLEANSE 1.

For now, destroying Nodes offers few strategic benefits, but learning how to do so is important. Many game mechanics will use them later.

Moving on, it’s time to manage time, resources, and opportunities for exploration on your own.

  • Play the next rounds until you open the next Door. Heroes may inspect Interactions, loot Chests, and replenish their resources. The only time limit to keep in mind is that Runes are drawn at the end of each round, and the Heroes are defeated when the bag runs out of Runes.

Once again, this is a free-play section of the tutorial.

There is still one final room in this tutorial, so ideally, save enough Runes for at least 4 rounds (6 Runes). The goal is to learn how to manage your resources and the pace of the Adventure.

You may leave this book aside for now and focus on the gameplay.

content.title: Bonuses and Class Abilities
content.body:
Passive and Triggered Bonuses

Many Skill, Class, and Equipment Abilities grant Passive Bonuses and Triggered Effects to the Heroes Actions. The terms and punctuation marks in each Ability’s text show how to manage them:

1) Dash (–): Separates the trigger from the effect. The text before the dash describes the trigger. The text after it describes the effect it casts when that trigger is met.

  • “AT THE BEGINNING OF YOUR TURN – SELF: SHIELD 2” means that at the beginning of each of your turns, your Hero gains SHIELD 2.
  • SURGE – This term means “Whenever you get a natural 16+ on a D20 roll during a ”.

2) Passive Bonuses improve the Hero’s actions or the effects they receive. The Ability’s text states whether it applies to actions you take or effects you receive:

  • CAST – When a Hero (or their Equipment) is the source of an effect, we say that they “cast” that effect.
  • RECEIVE – When a Hero is targeted by an effect, we say that they “receive” that effect.
  • Consumable Item effects are also CAST and/or RECEIVED by each Hero, as appropriate.

Most Passive Skills follow these conventions. There are exceptions, but the text usually explains itself in these cases, as in “YOUR MAXIMUM HEALTH INCREASES BY 4”.

Learning Class Abilities

Heroes also learn special abilities based on their Class–The Class Abilities.

Heroes can only learn Class Abilities that belong to their Class. Whenever a Hero learns a Class Ability, mark it using 1 White Cube.

Each Class Ability card represents an ability tree. Heroes always start an ability tree by learning the Level 1 Ability from it. Heroes can start a new tree whenever they learn a new Class Ability.

So, let's learn our first Class Ability.

  • Each Hero chooses one Class Ability tree and learns its Level 1 Ability.

Multiple Target Monsters

Some Monsters can hit more than one Hero with a single attack. This ability is described as “TWO TARGETS” on the Monster card. This feature introduces a small change to the Monster's behavior when "aiming" at their target.

Multi-Target Monsters prioritize hitting as many Heroes as they can. If they reach the same number of Heroes in different combinations, they prioritize the combination with the Strongest Hero among them.

By now, you should be ready to manage the round sequence and the rules for opening Doors—the bread and butter of a CoD Adventure.

  • Remove the End of the Round Game State Check-Up card from the Initiative Track.
    • Rounds continue as normal, and Doors can still only be opened if all Monsters are dead (although there are no more Doors to open). You may no longer need the card to guide you.

Growing Darkness and Hail To His Majesty remain on the Initiative Track, with the Scene Trigger card on top of the Rune card.

  • Play the next rounds until you kill all the Monsters so that the Hail To His Majesty Scene Trigger card triggers when it is ACTIVATED, leading you to the next stage of the Adventure.

Once again, this is a free-play section of the tutorial.

This is the first challenge in which you will open a Door, assemble a Setup, summon Monsters, and manage the rounds on your own, without any instructions. Once you can do this, you will have learned almost all of CoD’s basic mechanics.

You may leave this book aside for now and focus on the gameplay.

content.title: Hail to His Majesty
content.body:
Corrupted creatures laid siege to the city from the inside out, abducting villagers night after night to sacrifice them in a ritual to a dreadful entity. A classic tale.

When the last of the aberrations falls, the chorus goes silent and the world around you begins to tremble as if the ground were about to split in two. The shadows dance as if they’ve come to life, and you find it hard to describe what unfolds before your eyes.

“Hahaha! What is this?” echoes a hoarse laugh, coming from nowhere—sounding as if it emerged from a decaying corpse. Slowly, the darkness swirls and joins together to form a monster unlike anything you’ve ever seen before: fifteen feet tall, a crown on its head, and the spine of a giant wielded like a weapon by skeletal hands.

“Why resist? Everything that lives, sooner or later, dies. It’s not a matter of ‘if’, but ‘when’—and for you, that moment is now…”

First, place 4 Special Event tokens and the Undead King's model on the board as show below:

  • Place the Undead King’s model on Map E11-F, occupying the central emerald-colored area. If any Hero is in that area, they must reposition their model to a square adjacent to the villain.
  • Characters can no longer access previous Setup areas under any circumstances.

Then, make the preparations for your first Boss Fight:

  • Flip the second Monster Status Board (from orange to brown).
  • Set the Undead King’s starting Health. He has 25 HP for each Hero (for a total between 25 and 100).

Place the Undead King’s Monster card along with his 4 First Encounter Boss Attack cards, “FRONT” side up, on the Initiative Track.

You must place the 4 cards on the Track regardless of the Party size.

  • Replace the Hail to His Majesty Scene Trigger card with the Age of Darkness on the Initiative Track.
  • Each Hero repositions their model in one of the squares on Map DNE12-F.
  • Remove Bridge BR2-B from the board. Pets on the Bridge or previous Setups are Dispelled.

Boss Battles

Boss battles are epic moments in CoD gameplay.

In a way, the Setup and rules are the same as for Commanders. Bosses also have Attack cards.

Likewise, when they ACTIVATE their Boss Monster card, they MOVE and perform their Basic Attack. Conditions afflicting the Boss take effect in these turns.

If there is any doubt when resolving an Attack card from the Undead King, refer to the Clarifications section for them on page 16.

Focus Abilities

Heroes have special powers known as Focus Abilities.

  • Flip each Hero board to its Advanced side—this version features new Skills and the Focus Abilities.

When casting a Focus Ability, the Hero must discard the appropriate number of FOCUS tokens.

Casting a Focus Ability that is not a Reaction () costs a Minor Action. Focus Abilities that are Reactions () may only be used as Reactions.

The Range of made through Focus Abilities is set by the Weapon the Hero is wielding: Melee Weapons have Melee Range; Ranged Weapons have Range 1.

All other effects of Focus Abilities have Unlimited Range.

FOCUS tokens are Stackable Resources. Each Hero may have up to 4 of them at a time.

The final hour has come, and now you’re on your own.

  • Fight the Undead King until his Health is reduced to 0. Thanks to the Special Rule – “This Is Not Over Yet”, this will not end the fight, but it is the requirement for the Party to proceed to the next stage of the Adventure.
Special Rule – This is not Over Yet

When the Undead King’s Health is reduced to 0, he is not defeated yet. Skip all ACTIVATIONS of his Attack and Monster cards. All GRAPPLED Heroes are released. When the Initiative Marker reaches the Scene Trigger card, the Adventure will move to its next stage.

Once again, this is a free-play section of the tutorial.

You may leave this book aside for now and focus on the gameplay.

content.title: Age of Darkness
content.body:
The author of Blackriver’s misery is not a man. Not anymore. Now he is a carcass corrupted by the same unholy power he claims dominion over. Without a soul to long for anything, all he seeks is death and destruction.

“Who the hell are you?” the monster demands. The living usually don’t strike back. “You’re strong, I’ll admit that—but this ends now. The seeds have already been planted. There is no more escape, no more rest!”

Boulders fall from the ceiling as the Undead King raises his hands and makes the hall tremble once again. Your legs fight to stay grounded, but it is your mind that reels at the sight of a nightmare. Shadows condense like black clouds, flashing with emerald light. Then, like a storm, something warm and sticky as pitch spills into the hall.

The falling slime creeps along the floor and devours corpses with the hunger of a predator, sending a shiver down your spine. Flesh, entrails, and bones vanish in the blink of an eye, thickening and strengthening the mass that oozes ever closer.

“Welcome, mortals... to the Age of Darkness!”

The Undead King summons the Darkness to aid him. Prepare the second stage of this Boss Fight:

The Undead King restores 20 Health Points per Hero (for a total between 20 and 80).

Flip all of the Undead King’s Attack cards to their BACK side.

Flip Maps E8-B and E5-F. Remove any Special Event tokens from them, but leave all other elements as they are. Heroes are engulfed by Darkness and take damage (see ahead).

Place the Darkness Hunting Rune card at the bottom end of the Initiative Track, just above the Age of Darkness Scene Trigger card.

Replace the Age of Darkness Scene Trigger card with the Into the Underkeep Endgame Trigger card.

Darkness

Darkness is the main villain in CoD. Two rules are associated with it: how it is placed on the board (Spawns), and the effects it applies to both Monsters and Heroes.

Details can be found on page 44 to 45 of the Age of Darkness Rulebook (the blue one).

Spawning the Darkness

Darkness tiles spawns whenever a Rune is drawn due to the Darkness Hunting Rune card.

This is the Darkness Hunting Rune card. Each time it ACTIVATES, 1 or 2 Runes are drawn, spawning that many Darkness tiles on the board.

  • If 2 or more Runes are drawn at the same ACTIVATION, draw 1 at a time. The color of the Rune doesn't matter at this point.
  • The tile placed on the board follows the shape displayed at the back of the Rune drawn.
  • The tile must be placed on top of a Darkness Spawning Point, or next to another Darkness tile that is already on the board.
    • Darkness Maps count as Darkness tiles.
    • Players may position tiles however they want, but it must follow the Darkness behavior: reach the Strongest Hero, or get as close to them as possible.
  • If the tile does not fit on the board (or if it does fit but the fit is not in a position that is closest to the Strongest Hero), needs to change board levels or hang off a tray, it is split into 3 Small Darkness tiles instead.
    • The 3 Small Darkness tiles are placed trying to reach the Strongest Hero. If they succeed with the first or second tile placed, the remaining tiles are positioned to reach the next-Strongest Hero, and so on.
  • Darkness Tiles are not spawned if all Heroes are on Darkness tiles at the time a Rune is drawn.

Darkness Effects

Once on the board, Darkness becomes a Special Terrain. The first effects described are for “stepping” on it:

  • When a Hero steps onto Darkness, or ends their turn stepping in it, they take 2 non-preventable damage. This damage is only applied once per turn, which can happen more than once per round.

The next effects are “buffs” and “debuffs” that being on top of Darkness terrain applies to Characters:

  • Heroes receive a -2 TO HIT penalty to .
  • Monsters receive a +2 DMG bonus to their Basic Attack.
    • Large Monsters only need to be in 1 square of Darkness to receive this bonus.

Monsters seek the Darkness. Whenever they “aim” at a Target, if there is any Darkness square in which that Monster can end its movement without changing the Target, it will move to that square to benefit from this damage bonus.

Special Rule – This Is still not over yet

When the Undead King dies again, do not remove his model from the board or his cards from the Initiative Track. Skip all ACTIVATIONS from his Attack and Monster cards while he is in this suspended state.

Finally, the ultimate challenge has arrived.

  • Fight the Undead King until his Health is reduced to 0 again.

Once again, this is a free-play section of the tutorial.

You may leave this book aside for now and focus on the gameplay.

content.title: Into the Underkeep
content.body:
What takes place in the Great Hall is the embodiment of life’s struggle, as the adrenaline surging through your veins turns any dreams of wealth or glory into a single purpose: survival. Violence is met with violence, but in the end, the final blow is delivered by you.

“How... How can flesh surpass death?” the skeletal colossus murmurs as he collapses to the ground—but surprisingly, he laughs again. The black mass had already infiltrated the fortress’s foundations, shaking the ground harder than ever. “You know what? It doesn’t matter. You’ve won nothing but the right to dig your own graves...”

You barely have time to look at each other, let alone think of fleeing, before the cacophony of the collapse silences the hall, raising dust everywhere. All that’s left is to take a deep breath and hope for the best.

Surely, this job is turning out to be more costly than you expected…

Congratulations! You’ve completed the Drunagor Nights Season 01, Tutorial!

Proceed to the Adventure Underkeep Level 01 for your next game session—or if you prefer, replay this adventure in Advanced Mode first.

content.title: Clarifications – Stage 1
content.body:
First Encounter – Stage 1

Undead King’s Monster Card – The Undead King’s acts as a Large Monster. The Attack on this card gains bonus damage if the Undead King is standing on Darkness. If the Undead King ends his movement in an area with a Pile of Runes, UNRAVEL it: Return the Runes to the Initiative Track and the Undead King receives HEAL equal to the number of Runes times the number of Heroes (P).

Example: If there are 3 Runes in the Pile and 3 Heroes in the Party, he would recover 9 Health (3x3 = 9).

Death Rattle – The first effect draws 2 Runes. The second deals damage equal to the number of orange Runes on the Track to each Hero anywhere on the board (including GRAPPLED Heroes). Each Curse Cube those Heroes have reduces the damage taken by 1.

Example: If there are 5 orange Runes on the Initiative Track, this attack deals 2 damage to a Hero with 3 Curse Cubes (5 – 3 = 2).

NECROTIC BOLT – This attack deals damage equal to twice the number of Heroes in the Party to the Target Hero. The number of gray Runes on the Initiative Track has no effect.

Example: If there are 3 Heroes in the Party, this attack always deals 6 damage (2 × 3 = 6).

SHADOW WEAVE – The first effect creates a Pile of Runes in place of a Special Event token. The second causes each Pile of Runes to deal damage equal to the number of green Runes on the Initiative Track to each Hero within Range 1 of that Pile of Runes.

GRAVE GRASP – The first effect repositions the Undead King’s model to the area the Strongest Hero is in. Remove that Hero from the board, along with any other Heroes in the same area. This attack deals damage equal to the number of red Runes on the Initiative Track to each Hero removed this way. The second effect imposes a Special Condition: GRAPPLED. While GRAPPLED, Heroes are subject to the following rules:

  • They are Engaged in Combat.
  • They cannot use Reactions (), but can be targeted by them.
  • They cannot move, but may be targeted by SWAP effects.
  • They occupy the same square as the Undead King for Skill Range purposes (both targeting and being targeted). Whenever the Undead King moves, the Hero is carried along.
  • When released, the Hero is repositioned to a square adjacent to the Undead King.
  • GRAPPLED bypasses any Immunity to Conditions.

When the Undead King GRAPPLES a Hero, place a Curse Cube on the Undead King’s Health value at which they will be released: his current HP minus 15 (e.g., if he GRAPPLES at 36 HP, he releases at 21). If he GRAPPLES another Hero later, update the Curse Cube accordingly, applying the new value to all GRAPPLED Heroes. The Undead King always releases all GRAPPLED Heroes at the same time.

content.title: Clarifications – Stage 2
content.body:
First Encounter – Stage 2

ENERVATE – This attack deals damage equal to the number of orange Runes on the Initiative Track to the Strongest Hero at Any Range. Apply INTIMIDATE 4 to the target if they lose Health from this attack.

SHADOW JAUNT – The first effect draws 1 Rune, but no Darkness tile is spawned. The second effect repositions the Undead King’s model to the area where the Most Distant Hero is located. Each Character in that area is SHOVED, but only Heroes among them take damage. This attack deals damage equal to the number of gray Runes on the Initiative Track.

DEATH MATCH – The first effect creates a Pile of Runes in the space the Most Corrupted Hero is in, SHOVING them out of it. The second effect causes each Pile of Runes to deal damage equal to the number of green Runes on the Initiative Track to each Hero within Range 1 of that Pile of Runes. If a Hero loses Health due to this effect, they also receive CURSE 1. A Hero may be affected by multiple Piles in this way. Resolve each instance separately.

CORRUPT – The first effect draws 1 Rune, but no Darkness tile is spawned. The second effect repositions the Undead King’s model to the area the Strongest Hero is in. Each Character in that area is SHOVED, but only Heroes among them take damage. This attack deals damage equal to the number of red Runes on the Initiative Track.
